title_ar: حكم الاشتراك في التنقيب عن الذهب
title_en: The Ruling on Entering a Partnership for Gold Prospecting
body_ar: بالنسبة للذين يشتركون في التنقيب عن الذهب فبعضهم يوفر سيارة وبعضهم يوفر جهازا وبعضهم يوفر النفقة وبعضهم يشتغل بيده، هذا النوع من الشراكات هو من العقود الجديدة وليس من العقود المسماة وهو جائز إذا توافرت فيه الشروط ولم يقع فيه محظور شرعي فهو مثل ما كان يفعله الصحابة بإرسال خيلهم مع الغزاة فيسهم للفرس ويأخذ مالكها سهمها والفارس له سهم والفرس لها سهمان وهكذا، فيأخذ مالك الفرس نصيبه ويأخذ الفارس نصيبه وهكذا، فهذا النوع من الأمور الجائزة فهم شركاء فيه، وليس من أمور الغرر لأنهم لم يتشارطوا في ذلك شرطا معينا فإذا وجدوا شيئا فهو على القسمة التي اتفقوا عليها وإذا لم يجدوا شيئا فكل قد خسر فصاحب الجهاز وصاحب السيارة خسرا من تعطيل شغلهما وما بذل من سيارتهما وجهازهما والذي يعمل أيضا خسر من عمله ووقته وإذا ربحوا فهم في ذلك سواء لأنهم مشتركون فيه والنفع قد وصلوا إليه جميعا. أسأل الله أن يغنينا وإياكم أجمعين بحلاله عن حرامه بطاعته عن معصيته وبفضله عن من سواه، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله. اضغط هنا لمشاهدة الفتوى
body_en:
As regards those who enter into partnership in prospecting for gold — one of them provides a vehicle, one provides a device, one provides the expenses, and one works with his hands — this kind of partnership belongs to the new contracts and is not among the named contracts, and it is permissible (jāʾiz) if the conditions are met in it and no prohibition of the Sharia occurs in it.

It is like what the Companions used to do in sending their horses out with the raiding parties: a share was allotted for the horse, and its owner took its share, and the horseman had a share, and the horse had two shares, and so on. So the owner of the horse takes his portion and the horseman takes his portion, and so on.

This is of the permissible kind of matters, and they are partners in it. It does not belong to the matters of unacceptable uncertainty (gharar), because they did not stipulate any particular condition in it: if they find something, it goes by the division they agreed upon; and if they find nothing, then every one of them has lost — the owner of the device and the owner of the vehicle have lost by their work being suspended and by what they expended of their vehicle and their device, and the one who does the labour has likewise lost his labour and his time. And if they make a profit, they are equal in it, because they are partners in it and the benefit has reached all of them.

I ask God to enrich us and you, all of us, by what He has made lawful so that we need nothing He has forbidden, and by obedience to Him so that we need no disobedience, and by His bounty so that we need no one besides Him. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God.

flags.context: هو من العقود الجديدة وليس من العقود المسماة
options: the named contracts (the nominate contracts of the classical books)
the contracts with established names in the law
flags.note: العقود المسماة is a term of art: the contracts the jurists treat under fixed names — sale, lease, muḍārabah and the rest — as against contracts newly devised. The Sheikh's move is to say the arrangement is valid as an innominate contract on general principles rather than having to be forced into one of the named types. Not in the project glossary; a candidate for addition.

flags.context: وهو جائز إذا توافرت فيه الشروط
flags.note: جائز is used here of an act and a contract, so the legal sense applies and the kalām exemption in style guide section 8 does not. It is rendered 'permissible', with the Arabic bracketed to keep it distinct from مباح, which the corpus also renders 'permissible'. Note the Sheikh conditions the permission twice over: the conditions must be met, and no prohibition must occur — he does not enumerate either.

flags.arabic: فيسهم للفرس … والفارس له سهم والفرس لها سهمان
flags.context: the analogy from the Companions' practice with horses
options: reproduce the arithmetic exactly as given
note that the standard report gives the horseman one share and the horse two, totalling three
flags.note: The passage first says 'a share was allotted for the horse' and then that the horse has two shares, which reads as a compression rather than a contradiction: the point of the analogy is only that a contributed asset earns a share alongside the contributed labour. Reproduced as given without smoothing.

translator_notes: The ruling has two conditions attached that must travel with it: the conditions of a valid partnership must be met, and nothing forbidden may occur in it. The Sheikh does not list either, and nothing has been supplied.
His ground for excluding gharar is stated and should not be paraphrased away: no particular outcome was stipulated, so the parties share both the find and the loss.
The record says nothing about licensing, land rights or the environmental and safety questions that attend artisanal gold mining. Those are outside what he was asked.
The site-furniture line 'Click here to view the fatwa' closes the record and is preserved in body_ar, kept out of body_en.
